::: {#exr-radius}
## Radius of convergence

Consider the power series
$$
  \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{x^k}{2^k}
$$
with the partial sums $s_n(x)$ for $x = 1$ and $x = 3$

::: {.lm-sheet}
```{r}
n <- 0:8
s <- function(x) cumsum((x / 2)^n)
kable(data.frame(n = n, "x = 1" = s(1), "x = 3" = s(3), check.names = FALSE), digits = 4)
```
:::

Determine the radius of convergence and explain the table.

::: {.lm-solution}
With the ratio test, $\sum a_k x^k$ converges for $|x| < R = \lim |a_k / a_{k+1}|$. Here
$|a_k / a_{k+1}| = 2^{k+1} / 2^k = 2$, so $R = 2$.

For $x = 1$, inside the radius, the series is the geometric series with $q = 1/2$ and converges to
$1 / (1 - 1/2) = 2$. For $x = 3$, outside the radius, the terms $(3/2)^k$ grow, and the series diverges.
:::
:::
